introduction: Today we celebrate the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus. Moses tells Israel that God chose them not because they were great, but because he loved them. John tells us that God is love, and that he loved us first. In the Gospel, Jesus says, Come to me, all who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest, for I am gentle and humble of heart. Let us rest in the heart of Christ.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God loved us first and sent his Son for our salvation. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may reveal to the world the gentle and humble heart of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For priests, on this day of prayer for their sanctification: that their hearts may be formed by the heart of Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who labor and are burdened: that they may find rest in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel unloved or unworthy: that they may know that God chose them out of love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that, loved by God, we may love one another. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you loved us first and gave us the heart of your Son. Give rest to the weary, and teach us to love as he loves. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Come to me
reflection.body:
Moses tells the people why God chose them. It was not because they were numerous or strong: "for you were the fewest of all peoples; but because the LORD loves you." God's choice comes from love, not from our merit. And he is "the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness to a thousand generations."

John's first letter goes to the heart of the matter: "God is love." And he insists that love begins with God: "In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins." Our love is always an answer to his. "Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another."

In the Gospel, Jesus thanks his Father that the mysteries of the Kingdom have been revealed "to infants," to the simple and humble, rather than to the proud. Then he issues an invitation to everyone: "Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest."

He describes his own heart: "Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls." A yoke joins two animals so they can pull a load together. Jesus does not take away every burden, but he carries it with us. "For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."

The devotion to the Sacred Heart invites us to come to this gentle, humble heart with everything that weighs on us. It also invites us to let our own hearts become like his.

Today, bring your burdens to Jesus in prayer, one by one. Ask him to carry them with you. And let his gentleness and humility shape the way you treat someone who is tired or struggling.
